analysis:
Integration of all 14 units. The PR splits provider-side authorization readiness into a display path (displayedProviderAuthorization / displayedStatus) and a strict removal path (currentProviderAuthorization / currentStatus / removalReady). Status (StatusCommand.swift 135-140), both doctor paths (DoctorRunner.swift 37-38 and 78-79, DoctorCommand.swift 358-361 and 414-415) and the docs/changelog now show an unexpired App Attest lease even when the latest renewal is older than snapshotMaxAge. They pass the strict removalAuthorization separately to ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary. Positive MDM removal advice still requires the matching fresh decision and mdm_removal_ready, per the doc (provider-authorization.md 92-106) and the test descriptions. UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift (24-25) passes removalAuthorization: authorization and keeps removalReady(currentProviderAuthorization) as the gate (line 23). That gate is unchanged and fails closed. All code changes are local read-only CLI diagnostics. They do not touch the wire protocol, key custody, grants, revocation or the coordinator's final handoff checks (TB-002 authorizeInferenceHandoff, TB-011, T-052, T-053). Lease expiry still caps the displayed value. The worst plausible impact is a display-accuracy issue (T-058): a revoked or disconnected lease might read as authorized until expiry or the next state snapshot. That does not grant anything, and the coordinator independently rechecks. The removal-advice direction is conservative (T-057), so no concrete regression is supported.

Unverified, because source is outside the supplied evidence: the implementations of displayedProviderAuthorization, hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization, displayedStatus and summary. I could not confirm that the display path still enforces coordinator-URL binding, process identity, snapshot write freshness, revocation and NaN/infinite expiry, as the tests assert. I also could not confirm that no other caller uses the displayed value as a gate, or that the lease duration is bounded by the coordinator. The state-file lease is same-UID local data, so it cannot be trusted as evidence, which is consistent with the existing statement that local state cannot extend readiness. Integration replay was incomplete (53 units omitted), so I flag deeper review of the ProviderCore implementations. No threat-model update is needed from the supplied evidence.
